symptoms: Concentric circular brown spots ('target' rings) on lower foliage
Lower leaf yellowing and early defoliation
possibleCauses: Alternaria solani fungal spores splash-dispersed from damp soil
High canopy humidity and prolonged leaf wetness
management: Prune and destroy infected lower leaves immediately
Apply protective copper oxychloride or bio-control agent Trichoderma viride
Switch from overhead watering to drip irrigation to keep foliage dry
prevention: Rotate crops with non-solanaceous crops for 2-3 years
Maintain 60cm row spacing for good air circulation
Apply clean straw mulch around plant bases
expertAdvice: Monitor upper canopy. If lesions spread above mid-canopy or weather remains rainy, consult your local KVK extension officer.
disclaimer: Informational assessment based on image analysis. Always verify with local agricultural experts before applying chemical interventions.

symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with grayish-white centers and reddish-brown borders
Lesions coalescing causing leaf blighting and drying
possibleCauses: High nitrogen application coupled with cool nights and morning dew (>10 hrs)
management: Avoid top dressing with excess urea immediately
Apply university-recommended blast fungicide at early tillering stage
Maintain regulated water level without stagnant nitrogen runoff
prevention: Use certified blast-resistant cultivars (e.g., IR64 or regional hybrids)
expertAdvice: Critical outbreak risk. Field inspection recommended to rule out neck blast prior to heading.
disclaimer: Informational assessment based on image analysis. Consult official ICAR-IIRR advisories.

symptoms: Vigorous green leaves with intact margins
Normal square development without flaring or bore holes
No active pest colonies or fungal lesions observed
possibleCauses: Optimal soil moisture, balanced fertilization, and effective IPM monitoring
management: Continue regular scouting twice a week for early sucking pest or bollworm emergence
Maintain clean field borders and weed-free bunds
prevention: Install pheromone traps (5/acre) for early pest monitoring
Preserve natural beneficial predators like ladybird beetles and spiders
expertAdvice: Crop is in excellent physiological health. Maintain balanced nutrient schedule through boll development.
disclaimer: Routine image check. Regular field scouting is still advised during flower and boll formation.
